newsitem.title: UK: Iraq opposition group slams Iraq-Russia oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq opposition group slams Iraq-Russia oil deal.

text.p: An Iraqi opposition group on Thursday condemned a major oil deal between Iraq and Russia and said a future democratic Iraq would not honour agreements made between foreign oil companies and President Saddam Hussein.
"Deals with Saddam are morally indefensible and fiscally unwise," said an Iraqi National Congress (INC) statement quoting an INC letter to Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

Russia and Iraq signed last Friday a 23-year agreement worth $3.5 billion to develop seven billion to eight billion barrels of reserves in southern Iraq's west Qurnah oilfield once sanctions imposed by the United Nations after Iraq's invation of Kuwait are lifted.
Iraqi officials have said the deal would give Baghdad $70 billion in revenue -- more than enough for Baghdad to repay Moscow $7 billion in Soviet-era debt.

The INC said such agreements would only prolong Saddam in power because he would use the "greed of certain companies" as a lever to break out of the international isolation imposed during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
"The INC considers these agreements a tacit acceptance of Saddam's outlaw regime," the statement from the London office of the INC said.

"Saddam's regime will fall, sooner rather than later. Those companies and entities which are judged by a democratic government to have prolonged his dictatorship will have no place in Iraq's development."
